blocks.text: a cake, some cake, some cakes

O'zbekchada «Tort yedim» desak, butun tortni yedikmi, bir bo'lagini yedikmi yoki bir nechta pirojniy yedikmi — gapdan bilinmaydi, buni kontekst aytadi. Inglizchada esa ot oldidagi so'z buni aniq ko'rsatadi. Uch imkoniyat bor: **a / an** + sanaladigan birlik ot (bitta butun narsa), **some** + ko'plik ot (bir nechta), **some** + sanalmaydigan ot (bir oz, bir qism). 67-darsda otlarning ikki turini ko'rdik; bu darsda ular bilan **a** va **some** ni qanday tanlashni o'rganamiz.

**some** — aniq aytilmagan miqdor: «bir oz», «biroz», «bir nechta». O'zbekcha tarjimada u ko'pincha umuman ko'rinmaydi: I need **some water** — Menga suv kerak. **some** asosan darak gaplarda, shuningdek taklif va iltimosda ishlatiladi: Would you like **some tea**? Inkor va oddiy so'roq gapda odatda **any** keladi: I haven't got **any** money (76-dars). Sanaladigan birlik ot bilan **some** emas, **a / an**: **a** sandwich («some sandwich» emas).

items.text: She bought **some cakes** at the bakery.

blocks.text: Bir so'z — ikki ma'no: a chicken / chicken

Ko'p otlar ikkala turda ham ishlatiladi, lekin ma'nosi o'zgaradi. Qoida mantiqiy: butun, alohida narsa — sanaladigan; uning moddasi, bo'lagi yoki mavhum ma'nosi — sanalmaydigan. **a chicken** — tovuq (jonivor yoki butun tovuq), **chicken** — tovuq go'shti. **a paper** — gazeta, **paper** — qog'oz. **a glass** — stakan, **glass** — shisha (material). **a time** — marta, **time** — vaqt.

O'zbek o'quvchisi uchun eng qiyin guruh: o'zbekchada bu so'zlar bemalol sanaladi — «bir maslahat», «ikkita yangilik», «ma'lumotlar», «mebellar», «yuklar». Inglizchada esa ular **sanalmaydigan**: **a / an** olmaydi, `-s` olmaydi, fe'l birlikda. Bittasini ajratib aytish kerak bo'lsa — **a piece of**: **a piece of** advice, **a piece of** information, **a piece of** furniture. **news** oxiridagi `s` ga aldanmang — u ko'plik emas: The news **is** good.

rows: a lot of traffic, **a traffic jam**

blocks.text: Sifat qo'shilganda ham artikl paydo bo'lmaydi — bu eng ko'p uchraydigan xato: «What a nice weather!» emas, **What nice weather!**; «It's a good news» emas, **It's good news**; «a useful information» emas, **useful information**. Sifat otning turini o'zgartirmaydi: sanalmaydigan ot sifat bilan ham sanalmaydigan bo'lib qoladi.

items.text: Let me give you **a piece of advice**.

blocks.text: O'zbeklarning tipik xatolari: «He gave me an advice» → **He gave me some advice / a piece of advice**; «I need informations» → **I need some information**; «The news are bad» → **The news is bad**; «We bought new furnitures» → **We bought new furniture**; «What a terrible weather!» → **What terrible weather!**; «I've got many homeworks» → **I've got a lot of homework**.

Sanalmaydigan ot birlikdagi ot kabi ishlaydi: fe'l — **is / was / has**, olmosh — **it** («they» emas). Where's my luggage? — **It**'s in the car. Your advice **was** useful — I followed **it**. O'zbekchada «yuklarim», «ma'lumotlar» deb ko'plikda aytsak ham, inglizchada bitta butun massa sifatida qaraladi.

Ko'plik kerak bo'lsa — sanaladigan sinonimni toping: advice → **tips** (maslahatlar), furniture → **chairs, tables**, luggage → **bags, suitcases**, bread → **loaves**, homework → **exercises**, news → **stories**, work → **jobs**.

Bog'liq darslar: **some / any** — 76-dars; **much / many / a lot of** — 83-dars; **a little / a few** — 84-dars. Sanalmaydigan ot bilan **much** va **a little**, ko'plik bilan **many** va **a few** ishlatiladi.

rows: **a** chicken / chicken, **a** paper / paper, **a** time / time
advice, information, news, furniture, luggage, homework

examples.title: **a** cake, **some** cakes, **some** cake
examples.description: Bitta butun narsa — **a / an**; bir nechta — **some** + ko'plik; moddaning bir qismi — **some** + sanalmaydigan ot. O'zbekchada uchalasi ham ko'pincha bir xil aytiladi.

sentences.text: I bought **a cake** for Mum's birthday.
sentences.translation: Oyimning tug'ilgan kuniga **tort** sotib oldim.

sentences.text: There are **some cakes** in the fridge — help yourself.
sentences.translation: Muzlatgichda **pirojniylar** bor — olib yeyavering.

sentences.text: Would you like **some cake**? — Just a small piece, thanks.
sentences.translation: **Tortdan** olasizmi? — Kichkina bo'lagini, rahmat.

sentences.text: Madina is making **a salad** for the guests.
sentences.translation: Madina mehmonlar uchun **salat** tayyorlayapti.

sentences.text: Can I have **some salad** too? It looks delicious.
sentences.translation: Menga ham **salatdan** bering-chi? Juda mazali ko'rinyapti.

sentences.text: We picked **some apples** in Grandpa's garden.
sentences.translation: Bobomning bog'idan **bir nechta olma** terdik.

sentences.text: Aziz ate **an apple** and **some bread** before the lesson.
sentences.translation: Aziz darsdan oldin **bitta olma** va **ozgina non** yedi.

sentences.text: If you're hungry, there's **some soup** in the pot.
sentences.translation: Qorning och bo'lsa, qozonda **sho'rva** bor.

sentences.text: We ordered **two pizzas**, and there's still **some pizza** left.
sentences.translation: Biz **ikkita pitsa** buyurtma qildik, hali ham **pitsa** qolgan.

sentences.text: For school I need **a new notebook**, **some pens** and **some paper**.
sentences.translation: Maktab uchun menga **yangi daftar**, **bir nechta ruchka** va **qog'oz** kerak.

examples.title: **some** + uncountable: some milk, some time
examples.description: Sanalmaydigan ot bilan **some** — «bir oz», «biroz»: some milk, some money, some music, some time. Tarjimada ko'pincha ko'rinmaydi yoki «ozgina» bo'ladi.

sentences.text: Would you like **some tea** with lemon?
sentences.translation: Limonli **choy** ichasizmi?

sentences.text: Please buy **some milk** on your way home.
sentences.translation: Uyga qaytayotib **sut** olib kel, iltimos.

sentences.text: I need **some money** for the bus.
sentences.translation: Avtobusga **ozgina pul** kerak.

sentences.text: Put **some salt** in the water before you cook the pasta.
sentences.translation: Makaronni qaynatishdan oldin suvga **ozgina tuz** soling.

sentences.text: Dilnoza wants **some fresh air**, so she's going for a walk.
sentences.translation: Dilnoza **toza havodan** nafas olmoqchi, shuning uchun sayrga chiqyapti.

sentences.text: Could I have **some more plov**, please? It's delicious.
sentences.translation: Yana **ozgina osh** bersangiz? Juda mazali bo'libdi.

sentences.text: There's **some cheese** in the fridge, but there isn't any butter.
sentences.translation: Muzlatgichda **pishloq** bor, lekin sariyog' yo'q.

sentences.text: Sarah listened to **some music** and then went to bed.
sentences.translation: Sara biroz **musiqa** tingladi, keyin uxlashga yotdi.

sentences.text: These boxes are heavy — we need **some help**.
sentences.translation: Bu qutilar og'ir — bizga **yordam** kerak.

sentences.text: Before the exam Bekzod spent **some time** in the library, and now he feels ready.
sentences.translation: Imtihondan oldin Bekzod kutubxonada **biroz vaqt** o'tkazdi, endi o'zini tayyor his qilyapti.

examples.title: Two meanings: **a chicken** / **chicken**
examples.description: Bir so'z — ikki ma'no: **chickens** (tovuqlar) — **chicken** (tovuq go'shti), **a paper** (gazeta) — **paper** (qog'oz), **a glass** — **glass**, **a hair** — **hair**, **three times** — **time**.

sentences.text: My grandmother keeps **chickens** in her garden.
sentences.translation: Buvim hovlisida **tovuq** boqadi.

sentences.text: For dinner we're having **chicken** with rice.
sentences.translation: Kechki ovqatga guruch bilan **tovuq go'shti** yeymiz.

sentences.text: Dad buys **a paper** every morning on his way to work.
sentences.translation: Dadam har kuni ertalab ishga ketayotib **gazeta** sotib oladi.

sentences.text: The printer has run out of **paper** — can you bring some?
sentences.translation: Printerda **qog'oz** tugadi — olib kelolasizmi?

sentences.text: Is there **a clean glass**? I want some juice.
sentences.translation: **Toza stakan** bormi? Sharbat ichmoqchiman.

sentences.text: This table is made of **glass**, so be careful with it.
sentences.translation: Bu stol **shishadan** yasalgan, ehtiyot bo'ling.

sentences.text: Waiter, there's **a hair** in my soup!
sentences.translation: Ofitsiant, sho'rvamda **soch tolasi** bor!

sentences.text: Madina has got long dark **hair**, like her mother.
sentences.translation: Madinaning **sochi** onasinikiga o'xshab uzun va qora.

sentences.text: I've been to Samarkand **three times**, but this year I haven't got **time** to go again.
sentences.translation: Samarqandda **uch marta** bo'lganman, lekin bu yil yana borishga **vaqtim** yo'q.

sentences.text: Shall we have **a coffee** after the meeting? — Good idea, I drink a lot of **coffee**.
sentences.translation: Majlisdan keyin **bir chashka qahva** ichamizmi? — Yaxshi fikr, men ko'p **qahva** ichaman.

examples.title: **advice** and **information**: no **a**, no **-s**
examples.description: **advice** va **information** sanalmaydi: «an advice», «informations» deyilmaydi. Bittasi — **a piece of** advice / information; ko'pi — **some**, **a lot of**.

sentences.text: Can you give me **some advice** about universities in Britain?
sentences.translation: Britaniyadagi universitetlar haqida **maslahat** bera olasizmi?

sentences.text: My father gave me **a good piece of advice**: never be late.
sentences.translation: Otam menga **bir yaxshi maslahat** berdi: hech qachon kechikma.

sentences.text: Thanks for your **advice** — it was really useful.
sentences.translation: **Maslahatingiz** uchun rahmat — juda foydali bo'ldi.

sentences.text: We need more **information** about the hotel.
sentences.translation: Mehmonxona haqida ko'proq **ma'lumot** kerak.

sentences.text: Where can I get **information** about trains to Bukhara?
sentences.translation: Buxoroga poyezdlar haqida **ma'lumotni** qayerdan olsam bo'ladi?

sentences.text: The website has got **a lot of useful information** for tourists.
sentences.translation: Saytda sayyohlar uchun **juda ko'p foydali ma'lumot** bor.

sentences.text: Here's **an interesting piece of information**: the Tashkent metro opened in 1977.
sentences.translation: Mana **qiziq bir ma'lumot**: Toshkent metrosi 1977-yilda ochilgan.

sentences.text: I didn't ask for **advice** — I just wanted to talk!
sentences.translation: Men **maslahat** so'ramadim — shunchaki gaplashmoqchi edim!

sentences.text: Emma doesn't follow her doctor's **advice**, so her back still hurts.
sentences.translation: Emma shifokorining **maslahatiga** amal qilmaydi, shuning uchun beli hali ham og'riydi.

sentences.text: Sorry, I can't give you **any information** about the exam results until Friday.
sentences.translation: Kechirasiz, jumagacha imtihon natijalari haqida hech qanday **ma'lumot** bera olmayman.

examples.title: **news** and **weather**: good news, nice weather
examples.description: **news** — `-s` bilan tugasa ham birlik: the news **is**. **news** va **weather** sifat bilan ham artiklsiz: That's **great news**! What **lovely weather**!

sentences.text: I've got **some good news** — I passed my driving test!
sentences.translation: Sizga **xushxabarim** bor — haydovchilik imtihonidan o'tdim!

sentences.text: **The news is** on at nine o'clock.
sentences.translation: **Yangiliklar** soat to'qqizda beriladi.

sentences.text: That's **great news**! Congratulations!
sentences.translation: Bu **ajoyib yangilik**! Tabriklayman!

sentences.text: What **lovely weather** we're having this week!
sentences.translation: Bu hafta **havo** qanday **ajoyib**!

sentences.text: Is there **any news** from Bekzod? — No, nothing yet.
sentences.translation: Bekzoddan **biror xabar** bormi? — Yo'q, hali hech narsa yo'q.

sentences.text: **The weather** in Manchester is often wet and grey.
sentences.translation: Manchesterda **ob-havo** ko'pincha nam va bulutli bo'ladi.

sentences.text: I heard **an interesting piece of news** on the radio this morning.
sentences.translation: Bugun ertalab radioda **qiziq bir yangilik** eshitdim.

sentences.text: We had **terrible weather** on our holiday — it rained every day.
sentences.translation: Ta'tilda **havo** juda **yomon** bo'ldi — har kuni yomg'ir yog'di.

sentences.text: Mum, I've got **bad news**: I've lost my phone again.
sentences.translation: Oyi, **yomon xabar** bor: telefonimni yana yo'qotib qo'ydim.

sentences.text: In **good weather** we eat outside, but today it's cold and windy.
sentences.translation: **Havo yaxshi** bo'lsa, tashqarida ovqatlanamiz, lekin bugun sovuq va shamol.

examples.title: **furniture**, **luggage**, **homework**, **bread**
examples.description: O'zbekchada sanaladigan, inglizchada sanalmaydigan otlar: «mebellar», «yuklar», «uy vazifalari» emas — **furniture**, **luggage**, **homework**. Sanash uchun: a piece of furniture, a suitcase, a loaf.

sentences.text: We need **some new furniture** for the living room.
sentences.translation: Mehmonxonaga **yangi mebel** kerak.

sentences.text: Our flat is small, so we haven't got much **furniture**.
sentences.translation: Kvartiramiz kichkina, shuning uchun **mebelimiz** ko'p emas.

sentences.text: The only **piece of furniture** in the room was an old bed.
sentences.translation: Xonadagi yagona **mebel** eski karavot edi.

sentences.text: How much **luggage** have you got? — Just **one suitcase**.
sentences.translation: **Yukingiz** qancha? — Faqat **bitta chamadon**.

sentences.text: Please don't leave your **luggage** in the corridor.
sentences.translation: Iltimos, **yuklaringizni** yo'lakda qoldirmang.

sentences.text: Tonight Sarah has got a lot of **homework** for Monday.
sentences.translation: Bugun kechqurun Saraning dushanbaga **uy vazifasi** ko'p.

sentences.text: I've finished **my homework** — can I go out now?
sentences.translation: **Uy vazifamni** tugatdim — endi tashqariga chiqsam bo'ladimi?

sentences.text: There isn't any **bread** — can you buy **two loaves**?
sentences.translation: **Non** yo'q — **ikkita non** olib kelolasizmi?

sentences.text: At the airport they lost **one of my bags**, but the rest of my **luggage** arrived.
sentences.translation: Aeroportda **sumkalarimdan** birini yo'qotishdi, lekin qolgan **yuklarim** yetib keldi.

sentences.text: My uncle makes **wooden furniture** by hand, and people come from Tashkent to buy it.
sentences.translation: Amakim qo'lda **yog'och mebel** yasaydi, uni sotib olish uchun Toshkentdan ham odamlar kelishadi.

examples.title: Uncountable + **is** / **was** / **it**
examples.description: Sanalmaydigan ot bilan fe'l birlikda (**is**, **was**, **isn't**) va olmosh **it**: Where's my money? — **It's** in your jacket. Tasdiq va inkor yonma-yon.

sentences.text: Your **advice was** very helpful.
sentences.translation: **Maslahatingiz** juda foydali **bo'ldi**.

sentences.text: Where's my **money**? — **It's** in your jacket.
sentences.translation: **Pulim** qayerda? — **Kurtkangda**.

sentences.text: The **information** on this website **isn't** correct.
sentences.translation: Bu saytdagi **ma'lumot** **to'g'ri emas**.

sentences.text: Everybody was surprised by **the news**: **it was** on TV all day.
sentences.translation: **Yangilik** hammani hayron qoldirdi: **u** kun bo'yi televizorda ko'rsatildi.

sentences.text: This **bread is** fresh — **it** came from the bakery an hour ago.
sentences.translation: Bu **non** yangi — **u** bir soat oldin novvoyxonadan keldi.

sentences.text: Is the **luggage** ready? — Yes, **it's** in the car.
sentences.translation: **Yuklar** tayyormi? — Ha, **mashinada**.

sentences.text: **Traffic is** terrible in the morning, but **it isn't** bad at night.
sentences.translation: Ertalab **tirbandlik** dahshatli, lekin kechasi **unchalik emas**.

sentences.text: The **weather wasn't** good yesterday, but today **it's** sunny.
sentences.translation: Kecha **havo** yaxshi **emas edi**, bugun esa quyoshli.

sentences.text: Your **hair is** much shorter now — **it** looks great!
sentences.translation: **Sochingiz** ancha kalta bo'libdi — juda **yarashibdi**!

sentences.text: The **homework wasn't** difficult, so I finished **it** in twenty minutes.
sentences.translation: **Uy vazifasi** qiyin **emas edi**, shuning uchun uni yigirma daqiqada tugatdim.

examples.title: Dialogue: furniture for a new flat
examples.description: Aralash mustahkamlash: **furniture**, **advice**, **information**, **news**, **traffic**, **help** — sanalmaydigan otlar sifat bilan ham artiklsiz; sanaladigan **a bed**, **two chairs**.

sentences.text: — So, how's the new flat? Have you got any **furniture** yet?
sentences.translation: — Xo'sh, yangi kvartira qalay? **Mebel** oldingizmi?

sentences.text: — Only **a bed** and **two chairs**. Actually, we need **some advice**.
sentences.translation: — Faqat **karavot** va **ikkita stul**. Aslida, bizga **maslahat** kerak.

sentences.text: — Of course. What kind of **information** do you need?
sentences.translation: — Albatta. Qanday **ma'lumot** kerak?

sentences.text: — Where can we buy cheap **furniture** in Tashkent?
sentences.translation: — Toshkentda arzon **mebelni** qayerdan olsa bo'ladi?

sentences.text: — There's **a big market** near Sergeli with good prices.
sentences.translation: — Sergeli yaqinida narxlari yaxshi **katta bozor** bor.

sentences.text: — Thanks, that's **useful information**. Is it open on Sundays?
sentences.translation: — Rahmat, bu **foydali ma'lumot**. Yakshanba kunlari ochiqmi?

sentences.text: — Yes, but go early — **the traffic** is terrible after ten.
sentences.translation: — Ha, lekin erta boring — o'ndan keyin **tirbandlik** dahshatli bo'ladi.

sentences.text: — Good idea. Oh, and I've got **some news**: Madina is expecting a baby!
sentences.translation: — Yaxshi fikr. Aytgancha, **bir yangilik** bor: Madina farzand kutyapti!

sentences.text: — That's **wonderful news**! Give her my love.
sentences.translation: — Bu **ajoyib yangilik**! Unga mendan salom ayting.

sentences.text: — I will. And thanks again for **your help** — **it** means a lot to us.
sentences.translation: — Albatta. **Yordamingiz** uchun yana bir bor rahmat — bu biz uchun juda muhim.
